From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — Retail Bank

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our demo and a proposed POC plan so your team can review and confirm. I’ve attached a one-page POC plan (POC_plan_RetailBank_v1.pdf) and put an editable copy in the Drive link below.

Demo recap (high level):
- Showed Redwood hosted API + Dedicated routing options, live latency/cost short demo, and example evaluation harness for transaction categorization.
- Highlighted VPC/private deployment for regulated data and our rollout/fallback policies.
- Discussed realistic token throughput and expected cost per 1M tokens for your 50 RPS baseline.

Proposed POC objectives / success criteria:
1) Functional: Redwood returns correctly categorized transactions (precision >= 92% on your labeled holdout set).
2) Latency: 95th pct latency under 250ms for single-turn classification in Dedicated setup.
3) Integration: end-to-end pipeline ingesting a 1M-row sample into your staging environment using VPC peering or S3 signed URLs.
4) Ops: basic observability (per-route latency/cost) and alerting in Console.

Evaluation plan (3 weeks recommended):
- Week 0 (prep, 3 business days): exchange network details, sample dataset (10k), access controls, sign basic SOW/MSA.
- Week 1 (integration): connect sample dataset, validate end-to-end inference, baseline metrics.
- Week 2 (tuning & eval): iterate prompts/configs, run evaluation harness against labeled set, produce report.
- Week 3 (final): handoff and decision review (go/no-go).

Ownership:
- Redwood: Camila (AE) — program owner / timelines / procurement; Dylan (Solutions Eng) — technical lead for integration and eval harness.
- Retail Bank: Sam (PM) — success criteria owner; Priya (Eng Lead) — integration owner.

Next steps / asks:
1) Please review attached POC plan and confirm success criteria — any changes?
2) Share a short sample (10k rows) and a point of contact for network/team access (VPN/VPC details or S3 access).
3) Confirm whether legal prefers an MSA or an SOW to start (we can do a short SOW for the POC).
4) Proposed kickoff: Tue Jul 18 or Wed Jul 19 — which works for your team?

Links/attachments: POC_plan_RetailBank_v1.pdf (attached), editable copy: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xq_poc_retbank, HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deals/RDB-3245

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—

Hi Sam / Priya — adding technical details to answer your questions: 

- Connectivity: VPC peering or PrivateLink is our recommended approach for no-data-leak scenarios; setup time varies but is typically 3–5 business days with network teams. Signed S3 URLs are fastest to prototype (1–2 days) but require data to be staged to S3. For the POC I suggest starting with signed URLs (faster) and moving to VPC peering if you decide to expand.

- Schema: yes — transaction_id, timestamp, amount_cents, merchant_description, customer_id (hashed), label (for labeled set). We’ll provide a CSV template and an ingestion script as part of the POC artifacts.

- Security: attached is a short SOC2 summary (SOC2_summary.pdf). For full diligence we can schedule a call with our security team; we also support Private deployment (on-prem/VPC) if required for final evaluation.

Proposed kickoff and immediate next steps:
- Kickoff: Tue Jul 18 10:00am PT (we can send calendar invite).
- Deliverables week 0: signed POC SOW, sample dataset, network point of contact.
- I’ll prepare the eval harness and baseline tests (we’ll run them against your labeled holdout).

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if you want to go over the SOW language.

—Dylan
